speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me narrow this down, have these sensations been triggered specifically by changes in your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden, position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old woman without other neurological deficits or acute hearing loss is classic for BPPV.
